sections.h2: How is selling a house organized in Colorado?
sections.html:
Colorado sells houses county by county. The state has 64 counties, and two of them, Denver and Broomfield, are consolidated city and county governments. Each county has its own assessor, treasurer and clerk and recorder, so the office you call depends on where the house sits, not where you live.

That matters because the paperwork for a sale is split among three desks. The assessor values the property, the treasurer collects the tax bill, and the clerk and recorder records the deed. If you only remember one habit, make it this one: look up the county first, then call the office that matches the question.

Our county pages walk through the local offices. Examples include the Denver County recording guide, the El Paso County recording guide and the Arapahoe County property tax guide. The full list is further down this page.

sections.h2: What do Colorado property taxes and recording fees look like at sale?
sections.html:
Colorado bills property tax from the assessed value, not from your sale price. The assessor estimates actual value, a classification rate turns it into assessed value, and each taxing district applies its own mill levy. The state's Division of Property Taxation explains this in its published example. Our Colorado property tax guide covers appeals and unpaid bills in more depth.

Real property is revalued in odd numbered years, and notices of valuation go out by May 1. Taxes can be paid in full by April 30 or in two halves, due the last day of February and June 15. Overdue tax is collected through a tax lien sale, and a lien does not turn into a tax deed automatically.

Recording a deed carries a documentary fee. The statute sets it at one cent for each $100 of consideration, collected by the county clerk and recorder, and no fee is due when consideration is $500 or less. On a $250,000 sale that works out to $25. Recording fees on top of that vary by county, so check the clerk's schedule.

sections.h2: What happens if I fall behind and the lender starts foreclosure?
sections.html:
Most Colorado foreclosures run through the county public trustee, with a court order required before the sale. After the lender's file passes review, the public trustee records a Notice of Election and Demand. The auction is then set 110 to 125 calendar days after that recording, according to Eagle County's public trustee.

You still have options during that window.

  • File a Notice of Intent to Cure at least 15 days before the sale, then pay the cure amount in certified funds by noon the day before the auction.
  • Sell the house before the auction date and pay off the loan from the proceeds.
  • Ask the lender about reinstatement, a repayment plan, a loan modification, a short payoff or a deed in lieu.

Colorado Association of Realtors guidance says a hearing under Rule 120 happens before the auction, and the judge may sign the sale order if the borrower does not respond. The Eagle County trustee states that Colorado no longer gives owners a redemption period after the sale, so the weeks before the auction are the time to act. The Colorado Foreclosure Hotline is (877) 601-4673. If you are weighing a quick sale, our Colorado guides by city and county point to the local offices that handle the paperwork.

sections.h2: How does probate work when I inherit a house in Colorado?
sections.html:
Probate for a Colorado house is a district court case in the county where the owner lived. If the owner lived out of state, you can file in any Colorado county where they owned property. Denver cases go to the Denver Probate Court.

The Colorado Judicial Branch describes two paths. Informal probate is reviewed by the registrar with no hearing. Formal probate involves a court hearing and is required when you only have a copy of the will. The court cannot choose for you, so you pick the path yourself.

Once a personal representative is appointed, the clock starts on two duties: notify interested people within 30 days and file an inventory within 90 days. Nobody can sign a sale contract for the estate until someone holds that authority.

Two points help heirs plan. Colorado collects no estate or inheritance tax on deaths after December 31, 2004, according to the legislature's staff handbook. And a recorded beneficiary deed under C.R.S. 15-15-401 and following can pass a house on death outside probate. Read our probate guide, beneficiary deed guide and estate tax guide before you list or sign anything.

sections.h2: Does the homestead exemption affect a sale?
sections.html:
Colorado's homestead exemption protects part of your equity from a judgment creditor. Under C.R.S. 38-41-201 the amount is $250,000, or $350,000 when the occupant is elderly or disabled. The statute defines elderly as age 60 or older.

Do not confuse it with the property tax breaks for seniors. The senior exemption removes 50% of the first $200,000 of actual value for owners 65 or older who have lived in the home as a primary residence for at least 10 consecutive years. A senior deferral is a loan from the state that is recorded as a lien and must be repaid when the property is sold. Ask the county treasurer for a payoff figure early. Our homestead guide has the filing dates.

sections.h2: What if tenants live in the house I want to sell?
sections.html:
A tenant does not have to leave just because the owner decides to sell. Colorado evictions start with a written notice, and the court case can only be filed after the notice period ends. The Judicial Branch lists three notices.

  • Demand for Compliance (JDF 99 A): three to 30 days, set by the rental agreement.
  • Notice to Terminate Tenancy (JDF 99 B): one to 91 days for repeated or substantial violations.
  • Notice of No-Fault Eviction (JDF 99 C): at least 90 days, and one listed reason is selling the home.

Notices must be in the tenant's primary language. After a judgment, tenants usually get 48 hours, then the sheriff carries out a writ of restitution. Some tenants and landlords fall outside the no-fault rule, so confirm your situation with the court or an attorney. Buyers who take houses as-is can purchase with tenants in place, which is worth asking about. See our eviction process guide and landlord and tenant guide.

sections.h2: What does an as-is cash sale mean for a Colorado seller?
sections.html:
An as-is cash sale means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and pays without a mortgage. You skip repair work, and there is usually no lender appraisal to wait for. Cash Home Buyers works with owners across the state, and the closing itself still goes through a title or escrow company that records the deed with the county.

Before you accept any offer, check these items:

  • Who the buyer is, and what the contract says about the closing date and fees.
  • Any unpaid property tax, liens or a senior deferral that must be paid at closing.
  • Whether anyone else must sign, such as a spouse or co-heir.
  • Radon, since the Colorado health department reported that 44.6% of more than 80,000 household tests from 2008 to 2012 were above the EPA action level of 4 pCi/L. A test result can come up in any sale.

We do not promise a price here. Offers depend on the house, and you can ask your county office or an attorney any question about your own title.

faqs.q: How many counties does Colorado have?
faqs.a: Colorado has 64 counties, and Denver and Broomfield are consolidated city and county governments. Property tax, recording and probate all run through the county where the house sits.

faqs.q: What is the Colorado documentary fee on a home sale?
faqs.a: The statute sets it at one cent for each $100 of consideration, collected by the county clerk and recorder when a deed is recorded. No fee applies when consideration is $500 or less.

faqs.q: How long does a Colorado foreclosure take?
faqs.a: Per Eagle County's public trustee, the auction is set 110 to 125 calendar days after the Notice of Election and Demand is recorded. You can file a Notice of Intent to Cure at least 15 days before the sale.

faqs.q: Does Colorado have an estate tax?
faqs.a: No. Colorado collects no estate or inheritance tax on deaths after December 31, 2004. Large estates may still face federal rules.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate closes?
faqs.a: Only someone with authority, usually a personal representative appointed by the district court, can sign for the estate. A recorded beneficiary deed can pass title outside probate.

faqs.q: What does the Colorado homestead exemption protect?
faqs.a: It protects up to $250,000 of equity from judgment creditors, or $350,000 for an elderly or disabled occupant, under C.R.S. 38-41-201.

faqs.q: Can I sell with tenants in the house?
faqs.a: Yes, but the tenant's lease and notice rights still apply. A no-fault eviction notice requires at least 90 days, so ask a buyer whether they will purchase with tenants in place.
